description: Shared Renovate configuration of the package family. Every repository's .github/renovate.json (a family template) only extends it with github>JohnVerheij/assertions-ci//renovate/family.

packageRules.description: Force semver versioning for all NuGet dependencies. The nuget manager returns zero updates for them in this config (every dependency with a pending update is stuck: TUnit, SnapshotAssertions.TUnit, Meziantou.Analyzer), while semver resolves correctly, as proven by the doc-literal customManager. SonarAnalyzer.CSharp is re-excluded in the next rule.
Keep SonarAnalyzer.CSharp on nuget versioning: its 4-part version (for example 10.27.0.140913) is not valid semver, so it must use the nuget scheme, which resolves it correctly.
Commit convention `deps(nuget): ...` for NuGet bumps and the TUnit version-literal sync via customManagers (both resolve to the nuget datasource).

Override for `dotnet-sdk` (tracked via global.json). Renovate's nuget manager surfaces it, but it is the SDK itself, not a NuGet package; tag it as a CI/tooling concern with its own scope so PR titles read `ci(dotnet-sdk): ...`.
Commit convention `ci(github-actions): ...` for workflow action bumps.

Group the three TUnit packages (TUnit, TUnit.Assertions, TUnit.Core) into a single PR. They share a source repo and release in lockstep, so a single PR keeps Directory.Packages.props and the lock files internally consistent and avoids three partial-bump PRs per TUnit release.

Auto-merge non-major updates (patch, minor, digest, pin, pinDigest, lockFileMaintenance) once CI passes (requires 'Allow auto-merge' to be enabled on the repo). Major bumps stay manual. Digest is included because Renovate tracks SHA-pinned GitHub Actions as updateType 'digest' (not a semver category).

Packages that ship one version per .NET release. A package targets every supported .NET version, and each target framework takes the version of its own .NET release (conditional ItemGroups in Directory.Packages.props), so a new major belongs to a new target framework, added by hand under the TFM policy, never a bump of an existing entry: in the net10.0 group it would hand .NET 11 packages to .NET 10 consumers. Their major updates are therefore off, not waiting in the Dependency Dashboard; minor and patch updates stay automatic within each line. Package CI checks the same rule on what actually ships.

The SDK (global.json) and SourceLink (build-only, versioned with the SDK). A new major is deliberate: SDK 12 comes with .NET 12, and its SourceLink with it. Their major updates wait for approval in the Dependency Dashboard; minor and patch updates stay automatic.

customManagers.description: Keep the TUnit version literals (the Requirements line of every README, the smoke test's PackageReference, the bug-report Issue Form placeholder) in lockstep with the central TUnit package version. Renovate updates them in the same PR that bumps Directory.Packages.props.
